passage: Some people argue that handwriting is no longer worth teaching because students now type most of their schoolwork. But studies suggest that taking notes by hand helps students remember what they learn, perhaps because writing slowly forces them to summarize ideas rather than copy them word for word. Schools may therefore have good reason to keep handwriting in the curriculum.
stem: Which choice best states the main purpose of the text?
choices: To argue that handwriting still has value by pointing to research on how students learn
To explain the steps teachers use to help young students improve their handwriting
To describe how typing on computers has changed the way that students complete most of their schoolwork
To criticize students who prefer typing their notes to writing them by hand in class
steps: Sentence 1: an opposing view (stop teaching handwriting).
Sentence 3: the conclusion (schools should keep it).
So the purpose is to argue for handwriting using research.
There are no teaching steps, typing is only background, and the text criticizes no students.
key: Argumentative texts often state an opposing view, rebut it with evidence, then conclude.
